llm.summary: This vehicle-tracking skill is local and purpose-aligned, but it can save detailed vehicle, registration, insurance, and loan information in a JSON file.

dimensions.detail: Using a local data file is proportionate for a tracking skill, and no external transmission was found, but the stored fields can include sensitive personal and financial-adjacent details.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains Markdown instructions and eval files only; installation is documented as copying the skill folder into the OpenClaw skills directory and restarting the agent, with no scripts, packages, network fetches, or executable install steps found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation description is broad because it says to use the skill when anyone mentions common vehicle topics, which could invoke it in casual vehicle conversations even when the user did not clearly ask to track data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses storage in vehicle-data.json and instructs the agent to read and update it, but it does not define consent, redaction, deletion, file-permission, or minimization controls for VINs, plates, insurance notes, mechanic addresses, or loan details.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s stated purpose is vehicle ownership tracking, and its capabilities directly match that purpose: vehicle profiles, service history, maintenance schedules, mechanic contacts, admin deadlines, costs, and reminders.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable keeping vehicle records in a local JSON file. Avoid storing full VINs, plate numbers, insurance policy details, addresses, or loan information unless you need them, and periodically review or delete saved records you no longer want retained.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad invocation language is supported by the artifact and is worth user awareness, but it does not show hidden behavior or data use outside the vehicle-tracking purpose.
[SQP-2] expected: Persistent vehicle records are central to the skill and disclosed in the artifact; the missing privacy and retention controls are a caution rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[T09] expected: The plaintext local JSON storage and full-file load instruction are present in SKILL.md, but the artifact contains no executable payload, network exfiltration, credential handling, or deception.
